races.name: Wexford Town Mares Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a placed run of 2/16f/GOO in her record and 12 runs on similar going returning 1 win and 5 places; comes into this on a 10-day turnaround which is sharp but connections clearly have her ready, and she will need rivals to tire in front of her as the only true closer in the race.

runners_data.name: Farfromnowhere
runners_data.note: The controlling front-runner here, rated OR 125 and highest in the field, with Sean O'Keeffe aboard; 22 days since her last run and her Good-ground record of 7 runs returning 2 wins and 4 places is solid, though her STYLE_FIT tag at 0.92 flags she is being used in a slightly different role than her best — she is the engine of this race shape regardless.

runners_data.name: Full Of Life
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's OR 120 mare has a win and second on Good ground over this sort of trip and arrives 85 days fresh; her natural inclination is to race prominently but with Farfromnowhere dominating and La Note Verte also keen to go forward, she will likely find herself racing in a midfield position she does not naturally prefer, which softens her claims despite the quality of her record.

runners_data.name: Future Prospect
runners_data.note: Townend takes the ride on this Mullins-trained six-year-old who finished second on Good ground last time out — strong in theory — but like Full Of Life her true front-running style cannot be fully expressed here given how the shape is set; the paddling back to a tracking role means she relies on jumping well and Townend finding a good rhythm rather than getting the forward berth she thrives from.

runners_data.name: Kaylasjet
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with a going profile that is entirely unknown — flagged as a significant uncertainty; Ben Kennedy (7) takes the ride for a trainer with a single runner in the 14-day window and her form reads PP4-P suggesting she has not threatened yet, making her a speculative inclusion at best unless the race falls apart.

runners_data.name: La Note Verte
runners_data.note: Slevin partners this Mullins mare who has won three of her last seven on Good ground and finished third over an extended trip on Good last time; she is a natural prominent racer whose record over 16f on Good is excellent (3 wins, 4 places from 7 sim-going runs) and she is best-placed of the displaced forward types to actually secure a prominent position behind Farfromnowhere, giving her a strong profile for the dominant scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Farfromnowhere is the lone confirmed front-runner and will set the tempo from the outset over this 1m7½f trip on Good ground, with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead early — the pace will be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured or frenetic. La Note Verte is the most naturally prominent type capable of tracking Farfromnowhere in second or third, giving her a clean passage throughout, while Beauforts Storm will be held up off the pace as the only genuine hold-up runner in the field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position: Full Of Life and Future Prospect are both natural prominent racers but are displaced to midfield on the map, meaning one or both will need to settle for a tracking role rather than the forward berth they prefer, with La Note Verte best-placed to actually claim that position behind Farfromnowhere. A controlled, single-paced gallop set by Farfromnowhere on Good ground over this distance strongly favours horses who can track the leader in a prominent position and mount a sustained challenge from the second-last — the race shape tilts toward prominent-to-fore profiles, particularly those with clean recent form over similar trips on similar going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Farfromnowhere Controls, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Farfromnowhere sets a measured, uncontested gallop and a prominent tracker picks the right moment to challenge from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Farfromnowhere dictates from the front at a comfortable clip, with La Note Verte or Future Prospect tracking in second before mounting a sustained challenge between the final two fences; the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and sustained galloping ability rather than a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Farfromnowhere jumps cleanly throughout and the tempo is genuinely slow enough that no tracker can reel her in.
scenarios.body: Farfromnowhere uses her lead and jumping fluency to steal enough of a margin that rivals cannot close the gap on the run-in; Good ground and a small, lightly-competitive field makes the front-running task easier without a rival to push the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Outpaced Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected and the race develops into a proper test of stamina, leaving Beauforts Storm and hold-up types with ground to make up.
scenarios.body: With rivals stringing out behind Farfromnowhere under a stronger gallop, Beauforts Storm gets a positive tow into the race and is delivered with a late run; her Good-ground form over similar trips and her 2/16f/GOO placed run give her a live each-way claims if the race truly tests stamina late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the shape entirely, reducing the race to a lottery of who survives.
scenarios.body: In a small beginner's chase field with novice mares, a loose horse or a sequence of errors could scramble positions entirely and hand the race to whoever jumps most cleanly; Kaylasjet, with an unknown going profile and unproven form, could benefit from attrition reducing the field.

watchPoints.text: Watch Farfromnowhere at the early fences — if she jumps fluently and is allowed a soft lead, the race is set up as a front-runner's contest and any rivals who lose ground through jumping errors will have too much to do.

Future Prospect and Full Of Life are both natural prominent racers who cannot both get their favoured position; monitor the first bend to see which, if either, manages to track Farfromnowhere, as the one who does will be significantly better-placed than the one who drops back.

Kaylasjet is completely unknown on Going and lightly raced with no meaningful form — she is a safety risk in a beginner's chase and could affect the shape through jumping issues or erratic early positioning.

La Note Verte's 74-day break is worth noting — Mullins typically has horses ready on return, but watch her in the paddock and at the early fences for any signs of ring-rustiness before committing to her strong profile in the pace map.

Beauforts Storm's jockey Mr D Doyle carries a 7lb claim — at Wexford on Good ground in a small field of six, a patient hold-up ride will require precise timing from an amateur, and any misjudgement of pace could leave her with too much ground to make up on the run to the last.

races.name: Wexfordraces.ie Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Centreofattention
runners_data.note: Bolger runner with Harry Cobden booked, last run 12 days ago but recent form figures (/60-8P) are uninspiring; a natural hold-up horse whose position in the map is the product of the field's congested rear, meaning he may end up closer than ideal and unable to produce his best finish.

runners_data.name: Coul Dreamer
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground in flat-race code and placed three times at that level but this is a step up in jump-racing class; five years old and lightly campaigned over fences, his natural waiting style is cramped by a field with no genuine pace to sit off, which undermines his chance.

runners_data.name: Jet Setting Jim
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the key pace-setter; 294 days off is a significant concern for a nine-year-old with a headgear notation, but he has solid Good-ground credentials (13/15 sim-going runs show experience) and if his schooling has been sharp he could dictate throughout on a track that suits controlled front-runners.

runners_data.name: Killeemore Lad
runners_data.note: 745 days off the track is an enormous absence flag, but prior form at this distance on Good ground is excellent (1W5P in similar going, back-to-back placed efforts at 16-17f); trained by the same yard as Jet Setting Jim and a genuine hold-up horse who may capitalise if he retains any of his old ability — the fitness query is the only obstacle.

runners_data.name: Silent Selector
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good and has course experience, though OR 120 puts him at the bottom of the class range; Philip Donovan rides for a trainer with 0/4 in the 14-day window, and his natural hold-up style faces the same late-run challenges that all the closers face in this slow-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Sky Lord
runners_data.note: De Bromhead/O'Keeffe is a potent combination and Sky Lord has four consecutive placed efforts to his name, suggesting consistency without the winning punch; tongue-strap fitted, and his GOO-ground placings are encouraging, but he needs a stronger pace than Jet Setting Jim alone is likely to generate to deliver his best.

runners_data.name: Where Are You Now
runners_data.note: Bolger's second runner, ridden by a 3lb claimer, with recent form including a P; naturally prominent but has been running over much longer trips (22-24f) and drops to 15f here — the trip drop could sharpen him up or he may simply lack the class to capitalise on a prominent pitch.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: Won at 16f on Good and placed on the same surface, giving him the most relevant form profile among the prominent types; Daniel King has ridden him before and the horse travels in headgear (t), suggesting he needs to be kept up to his work — if he reproduces his best, he has a tactical case in this slow-pace scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Jet Setting Jim is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press him from the off, he should be permitted to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable clip over this 1m7½f trip on Good ground at Wexford. Where Are You Now and William Tell are the only other horses with prominent tendencies and neither carries the profile of a horse that will aggressively dispute the lead, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured in the early stages. The field does hold more hold-up and wait-and-pounce types than the map can accommodate naturally — Killeemore Lad, Coul Dreamer, and Centreofattention are genuine off-the-pace horses who may find themselves racing closer to the pace than ideal simply because the race lacks the tempo to string them out; Killeemore Lad is most likely to find a position from which he can strike, given his course profile and fitness credentials. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling a moderate gallop — most favours prominent-to-midfield horses with proven Good-ground form at this sort of distance, who can travel smoothly into position and pounce when Jet Setting Jim is challenged from the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jet Setting Jim Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Jet Setting Jim is allowed to roll along uncontested and sets a measured, confidence-building gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: He dictates every yard, jumps fluently, and the modest pace compresses the field, neutralising the hold-up horses who need a searching test; horses who can travel prominently behind him and stay close enough to strike from two out are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the second-line prominent horses tracks Jet Setting Jim closely and delivers a timely challenge at the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: William Tell or Where Are You Now moves into a striking position before the home straight, negating Jet Setting Jim's jump advantage and hitting the front before the hold-up horses can close; Good ground suits both and the compressed pace means they never had to over-exert early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses turning for home and the closers get a clear run through from midfield in the final two fences.
scenarios.body: Sky Lord or Silent Selector, both proven finishers on Good ground, benefit from a bunched field and produce a late surge if the front two tire; this shape requires the pace to have been genuinely strong enough to soften Jet Setting Jim, which the data suggests is unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Jet Setting Jim's 294-day absence causes a jumping error or his fractions become ragged, creating a cavalry charge finish.
scenarios.body: A wide-open scramble up the home straight suits the freshest horse on the day regardless of style; Killeemore Lad and Coul Dreamer both carry fitness arguments that could see them capitalise on disruption.

watchPoints.text: Killeemore Lad — 745 days off the track is extreme; watch the market closely pre-race to gauge yard confidence, as a well-backed return would significantly upgrade his chance.
Jet Setting Jim — 294-day absence from a nine-year-old with headgear means his jumping sharpness at the first fence is critical; a clumsy early jump could unsettle the entire race shape.

Sky Lord — watch whether O'Keeffe sends him forward unusually early given the lack of genuine pace; De Bromhead horses often travel prominently when conditions allow, which would shift Sky Lord out of his mapped position.

Killeemore Lad and Jet Setting Jim share the same trainer (Andrew Slattery) — watch for any stable tactics that involve Killeemore Lad being covered up behind his stablemate rather than tracking freely, as that could compress the field further and favour closers.
Good ground across the entire card is confirmed and consistent — no horse in this field carries a going concern, so the pace map rather than the ground is the dominant analytical variable today.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Trasna Na Pairce
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who is most effective when allowed to bowl along unchallenged; De Bromhead in strong form (5/30), Dylan Whelan (4) claims 4lb, and the Good going suits (12 of 14 sim-going runs placed or better) — the key question is whether she can hold her lead when challengers arrive at the second-last.

runners_data.name: Mercury Mission
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a productive record on Good going at around 16f (three wins/places in last four on similar surface); P Cluskey yard is cold (0/1 T14) but the horse arrives fresh at 22 days, and if he tracks the leader at close quarters he is well-positioned to capitalise on any late weakness.

runners_data.name: Tuckmill
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old prominent racer returning after 83 days off; the blinkers are fitted, Fahey stable is 0/10 over 14 days suggesting a quiet patch, and recent form figures (0, P, 7) make it hard to be confident even if he does get his natural position close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with an excellent record on Good ground — all six sim-going runs have produced a win or place — and arrives 54 days fresh under De Bromhead (5/30 T14); needs others to go fast enough to close the gap jumping the last, which is not guaranteed in this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Tequila Talkin'
runners_data.note: A front-running type by nature who is likely to find himself further back than ideal given the prominent runners ahead of him in the betting; his best form at 16f Good suggests he wants to race handily, so being shuffled into midfield is a material disadvantage, though the 22-day turnaround is fine.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: Has won and been placed at 18f on Good ground and is genuinely suited by this trip; tongue tie and cheekpieces fitted, but as a natural prominent racer she may struggle to secure her preferred position with Trasna Na Pairce and Mercury Mission already ahead — if she does get cover just off the pace she becomes a live contender.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: Front-running type by inclination but all five recent runs on Good over 20f have produced modest finishes (best a fifth); the P J Rothwell yard has one winner from 21 runners over 14 days, the 72-day break is a minor flag, and being pushed back from his natural berth makes a forward display unlikely.

races.paceDynamic: Trasna Na Pairce is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with only Mercury Mission and Tuckmill likely to press from prominent positions, she faces minimal direct pressure and should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop throughout. On Good ground over 1m7½f at Wexford — a sharp, turning track that rewards those on the pace — a controlled lead from Trasna Na Pairce sets up a race that is unlikely to be run at a searching tempo. This shape strongly favours horses that can travel close to the pace and pick up over the final two fences, making prominent or close-tracking runners the primary beneficiaries; deep hold-up horses face too much ground to make up on a track that does not truly test stamina. The field contains more genuinely prominent types than the map can accommodate — Tequila Talkin', Stoneyford Lady, and Ballybrittas are all natural front-to-midfield runners but will be shuffled back in the race shape; of those three, Stoneyford Lady — who has the best class profile at the trip and has won at 18f Good — is most likely to find a prominent berth, with Tequila Talkin' the next most capable of asserting early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trasna Na Pairce Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce leads at a comfortable tempo and Mercury Mission or Tuckmill sit in behind without applying pressure.
scenarios.body: Trasna Na Pairce dictates the fractions, the race stays at a steady gallop, and those positioned second or third in the early running have first run on the field jumping the last; prominent types with stamina for the trip can go past a leader that has had an easy time in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the race becomes a sprint from the second-last fence, allowing a fresh-legged finisher to close.
scenarios.body: Lady Doyanne, a genuine hold-up type with a solid record on Good ground (6 runs, won and placed in similar conditions), could swoop late if the tempo collapses; her De Bromhead yard is in form (5/30 over 14 days) and she arrives fresh off a 54-day break.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed prominent types force a stronger pace than expected, creating a true-run race that filters out the weakest jumpers.
scenarios.body: Stoneyford Lady and Tequila Talkin' both push forward to contest the early gallop, the pace lifts, and the race sorts itself out on merit over the final three fences; horses with higher class figures and clean jumping round a sharp track like Wexford are rewarded.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Fades
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce goes too fast for the conditions or makes a jumping error that bleeds her momentum in the final circuit.
scenarios.body: With the leader weakening between the last two fences, Mercury Mission or Tuckmill — positioned closest — inherit the lead, but their own limitations at this level mean the door opens for any runner who has been tracking them quietly throughout.

watchPoints.text: Stoneyford Lady — watch the first two furlongs to see whether Danny Power (4) pushes forward early; if she gets a prominent berth against her natural inclination she becomes a serious threat, but if she is checked back she faces an uphill task on this sharp track.

Trasna Na Pairce — any jumping error at the open ditch or the water, or signs of her being headed before the second-last, would dramatically change the race shape and open the door for the hold-up horses who currently trail her.

Tequila Talkin' and Ballybrittas — both are natural front-runners likely to be racing out of their comfort zone in midfield; watch whether either fights for position early and creates a faster-than-expected tempo, which would favour Lady Doyanne late.

Lady Doyanne — her finishing position will be heavily dependent on the pace set by Trasna Na Pairce; if the early gallop is modest, watch her response at the second-last where she typically needs a two-fence run to bridge the gap from behind.

Tuckmill — the blinkers suggest a trainer seeking more early energy from a 10-year-old returning after 83 days; if he jumps cleanly and sits prominent, his presence could subtly lift the pace and make this a more genuinely run contest than the lone-front-runner map suggests.

races.name: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Farrokh
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with strong Good-ground form (8 placed runs from 15 similar-ground starts); 244 days off is a notable concern, and at OR 99 he carries top weight, but if fit he controls the shape of this race entirely from the front.

runners_data.name: Keep On Dreaming
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden in the saddle adds significant jockey class for trainer E Bolger; only 2 from 5 runs on Good ground suggests a slight preference for softer, and the 44-day absence needs monitoring, but OR 99 and a recent win give him obvious claims from the rear.

runners_data.name: Justicialism
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with five places in his last eight Good-ground runs and a preference for this trip range; the tongue-tie is retained, he's fresh off a 26-day break, and his record of 0 wins from many places suggests he needs everything to fall right to convert.

runners_data.name: Arctic Piper
runners_data.note: A 195-day absence is a significant fitness question mark for this hold-up type; form has been poor (P, 8, P in recent starts) and his best going appears to be Heavy or Soft rather than Good, making this a tough assignment on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Quinn The Eskimo
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted and a 5lb claimer aboard — the combination needs to work in tandem; Good-ground form is limited (1 win, 1 place from 13 runs) and he has had jumping issues (U in recent form), making him a risky proposition despite the low weight.

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: Won last time out at OR 91 on Good ground over this trip, so the form is current and relevant; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, he is mapped to midfield here because the rear of the field is oversubscribed — that positional compromise is a real concern given his usual waiting tactics.

runners_data.name: L'Amiral Fromentin
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a placed record at this level on Good ground (3 placed from 10 similar runs) for the in-form Rothwell yard (1 from 21 over 14 days); his natural running style is rear-of-field but he has been shifted forward on the map through necessity, which may suit this pace shape better than it first appears.

runners_data.name: King's Son
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin takes the ride for a lightly-raced six-year-old showing improvement (3rd and 6th in last two); Good ground and a step back down in trip from recent outings could help, and a prominent style suits the expected race shape well.

runners_data.name: Getaway Henry
runners_data.note: Won 12 days ago at OR 86 on Good ground over a similar trip — very current form; headgear noted (p), carries the penalty confidently, and his prominent style is perfectly suited to the likely pace scenario set up by Farrokh.

runners_data.name: Only A Dollar
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, placed on the map further forward than ideal because the genuine back-markers are numerous; Good-ground form is modest (1 win, 2 places from 15 runs) and the 53-day absence adds another question, making him one to use only in chaos-dependent scenarios.

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with a placed record on Good ground; six-year-old who has been running over this course configuration and handles the track, though trainer Crowley has no runners in the 14-day window and the OR 86 mark means she needs improvement to trouble the front rank.

runners_data.name: Dunany Point
runners_data.note: Form includes a P (pulled up) last time and a string of mid-pack finishes; Good-ground form shows 1 win and 4 places from 15 runs so she handles conditions, but the prominent style will need to function better than it has in recent races for this to be a winning run.

runners_data.name: Dontdooddson
runners_data.note: A 13-year-old veteran at OR 72 who is a natural prominent racer — the field's depth means he is unlikely to secure that position and will operate further back than comfortable; his last five runs have all produced 7th-place finishes bar one, and age and weight of evidence suggest he is best watched here.

races.paceDynamic: Farrokh is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap chase and, with no genuine rival to push him for the lead from the off, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Wexford's flat, right-handed track. Behind him, King's Son, Getaway Henry, Polly Poppins, and Dunany Point are all natural prominent racers who will attempt to track closely, creating a competitive early order without necessarily forcing a breakneck tempo. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically all secure their favoured positions — Dontdooddson is a natural prominent horse who is likely to find himself shuffled further back than ideal, while Chosen Shant and L'Amiral Fromentin, both true hold-up types, have been mapped to midfield simply because the rear is overcrowded, meaning their usual finishing kick may be compromised. A moderate, even pace set by one unchallenged leader on Good ground over an honest but not excessive trip strongly favours prominent-to-handy types who can travel with the early pace and produce a clean, well-timed challenge from the second half of the race — closers reliant on a genuine end-to-end burn are disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Farrokh Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Farrokh sets a fair but unforced gallop and the prominent horses behind travel sweetly throughout.
scenarios.body: Farrokh dictates from the front at a comfortable clip, allowing King's Son, Getaway Henry, or Polly Poppins to track him into the straight with reserves intact before producing a decisive challenge at the last. Good ground and a steady tempo suit horses who can race handily without burning energy early, and this profile punishes true hold-up types who need a faster early pace to generate late momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the steady gallop means the race becomes a sprint finish and one of the true hold-up types finds a clear run late.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow pace compresses the field into the straight and turns the race into a jumping test rather than a stamina contest, which could allow Justicialism or Keep On Dreaming — both confirmed hold-up horses — to finish powerfully past tiring rivals. Justicialism has been placed in five of his last eight runs on Good ground and handles this trip well, while Keep On Dreaming's class gives him a live each-way chance if he travels into the race from the rear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up, Leader Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop increases markedly from the halfway point and Farrokh proves strong enough to grind rivals into submission.
scenarios.body: Farrokh has strong Good-ground form (15 appearances, 8 placed) and at OR 99 has the class to exploit a race where the early pace suits him uniquely; if he kicks on turning in and opens a decisive advantage, rivals who have been chasing him throughout will find it hard to reel him in. This scenario particularly hurts redistributed prominent horses like Dontdooddson who will have lost ground positionally and lack the finishing gears to close on a well-placed front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors and scrimmaging in the chasing pack cause multiple horses to lose their position, creating a wide-open finish.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners over fences on a tight track, fallers, unseated riders, or interference can scramble the race order entirely, opening the door for a horse like Quinn The Eskimo or Only A Dollar to pick through the wreckage at long odds. Both sit at the lower end of the handicap, carry lighter weights, and could benefit from a reduced field if incidents thin the competition in front of them.

watchPoints.text: Getaway Henry won 12 days ago and races off a penalty — watch whether he is fresh enough to back up quickly, as his prominent style perfectly suits the expected pace but a quick turnaround at age nine can backfire over fences.

Farrokh's 244-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — if he comes back short of peak fitness and fades after the second-last, the entire pace scenario collapses and hold-up horses like Justicialism and Keep On Dreaming become live threats.

Chosen Shant and L'Amiral Fromentin are being mapped to midfield despite being natural hold-up horses — watch the early stages to see whether they slot into their genuine rear-of-field position, which would mean their probability in a pace-collapse scenario rises sharply.

With 13 runners over fences on a relatively tight Wexford circuit, watch for crowding at the early fences — Quinn The Eskimo has an unseated rider in recent form and Arctic Piper is returning from 195 days off, making both potential jumping risks that could unsettle those around them.

King's Son with JJ Slevin is worth tracking through the race — Slevin is an aggressive jockey who may push for a prominent position early, and if he gets the jump on Getaway Henry and Polly Poppins for the tracking role behind Farrokh, he could prove the most dangerous of the prominent challengers.

races.name: Wexford Quay Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Boston Jury
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a significant booking for this Gordon Elliott-trained six-year-old, whose hold-up style requires a true gallop to deliver — sim-going record of 8/10 on Good is encouraging but recent finishes of 6-8-9 suggest he needs things to fall right.|

runners_data.name: Figurehead
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old whose recent form figures of 0 and 6 on Good ground make for sobering reading; hold-up style means he needs pace to hunt down, and his sim-going record of 9/15 finishes suggests he finds this ground consistently unrewarding.|

runners_data.name: Glenashling
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's seven-year-old has a solid placing record (1W3P in sim-going) and ran second at 17f on Good recently, but a hold-up profile in a race with a single controlled front-runner means he may lack the trigger to land a winning challenge.|

runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground at OR 120 and arrives fresh off 19 days, but this natural front-runner or prominent racer is squeezed out of his preferred berth by the sheer volume of pace in the field — his OR 120 and previous wins mark him as a class act, yet he will likely race further back than suits.|

runners_data.name: Kool One
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with three wins in sim-going and genuine prominent racing style, Kool One is one of the runners best placed to actually secure a berth on the pace; his last run was 59 days ago and he has limited experience at this trip, but the Good ground ticks a box.|

runners_data.name: Los Blanco
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old has a win and a second in his most recent sim-going runs, races prominently, and Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking — 84 days off is worth monitoring but all his best form is on Good or Soft ground at this sort of trip.|

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: Daniel King rides this prominent-style eight-year-old who finished second last time out on Good over 20f — his sim-going record of 3/14 with just one placing is a concern, suggesting he shows well without converting, but his recent runner-up is form to note.|

runners_data.name: Now So Jake
runners_data.note: Has been off 720 days — the layoff is the dominant fact here; he showed smart form previously with wins on Good ground but beginners' chase fitness after that absence is a serious unknown despite a prominent racing style that suits this shape.|

runners_data.name: West Away
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old returning after 208 days for a small yard (T14: 1/1), and a natural prominent racer who is pushed back by the weight of pace in this field; sim-going record of 10/15 is moderate and the combination of absence and positional compromise makes him a significant risk.|

runners_data.name: Clody Diamond
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's six-year-old is a genuine front-running or prominent type who arrives 22 days fresh, but the crowded pace picture means she is unlikely to dictate as she would prefer — her best run was a second on Good ground and she is down to 159lbs, but racing against her style is the core concern.|

runners_data.name: Colleen Danu
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground at 20f and has placed three times in sim-going conditions, making her one of the more interesting runners on form — she is a natural front-runner who will struggle to get to the front here, but if the field strings out she could be better placed than her mapped position implies.|

runners_data.name: Queenofthelodge
runners_data.note: The confirmed leader and a filly on 159lbs, she holds a strong Good-ground profile (sim-going 12/15, 3W7P) and will face no serious early challenger — the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is mapped to a role that stretches her, but in terms of actual race position she is perfectly placed to control this.|

races.paceDynamic: Queenofthelodge is the confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, she will be allowed to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m3f. The prominent pack — Los Blanco, Kool One, Mickie Angel, and Now So Jake — will slot in behind her, but Jackson Lamb, Colleen Danu, Clody Diamond, and West Away are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all get their preferred position in a field this congested, meaning several will be shuffled back against their nature. The hold-up horses Boston Jury, Glenashling, and Figurehead will settle at the rear and need a meaningful injection of pace to bring them into play, which one uncontested front-runner at a moderate clip is unlikely to provide. This race shape — a single leader dictating at a sustainable tempo with a jostling prominent pack — strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace and produce a clean jumping round rather than those relying on a sprint finish from deep, making genuine prominent racers and the neater jumpers the clear tactical beneficiaries. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can realistically secure that berth; of those, Los Blanco, Kool One, and Mickie Angel are best placed to naturally occupy the prominent positions, while Jackson Lamb, Colleen Danu, Clody Diamond, and West Away are the likeliest to find themselves racing further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Queenofthelodge Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Queenofthelodge sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is decided by who travels best in the prominent group.
scenarios.body: Queenofthelodge dictates from the front at a comfortable tempo, and the horses who settle just behind her — Los Blanco, Kool One, Mickie Angel — have the cleanest route through without having to overextend; the winner will be whichever of those can jump fluently and sustain their effort up the run-in on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Compression, Hold-Ups Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Queenofthelodge's lead is pegged back and early jostling for prominent positions creates a compressed, even gallop that plays into the hands of patient hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Boston Jury and Glenashling, both legitimate hold-up types with Good-ground form, are able to close the gap when the pace steadies late; Jack Kennedy's positional intelligence on Boston Jury in particular could prove decisive if the field bunches through the final circuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Surprise Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the volume of displaced prominent types disrupts the race pattern mid-race — interference, jumping errors, or a false pace — and one of the redistributed horses manages to reclaim their natural front position.
scenarios.body: Jackson Lamb or Colleen Danu, both genuinely well-rated at OR 120 with winning form on Good ground, would be significantly more dangerous if they can override the traffic and race where they want; their form suggests class enough to capitalise if the race falls apart around them, though racing out of role remains the default risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Queenofthelodge Front-to-Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves so moderate that Queenofthelodge is never seriously challenged and simply leads throughout unchallenged to the line.
scenarios.body: On a flat, right-handed track like Wexford where front-runners can get an easy time of it and 2m3f does not overly test stamina, a wire-to-wire performance is plausible if the prominent pack fails to organise; Queenofthelodge's Good-ground profile (sim-going 12/15 with 3W7P) underpins the threat, though the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence slightly.

watchPoints.text: Queenofthelodge takes the field along unchallenged from the front — if she meets every fence cleanly through the first circuit, she could be very difficult to peg back on this flat track at a moderate tempo.

Los Blanco and Kool One are the prominent horses best positioned to race in their natural style; watch how quickly they settle behind the leader — if either gets a clean jump at the first few fences, they become the most direct dangers.

Jackson Lamb and Colleen Danu are both OR 120 horses racing out of their natural prominent roles — if either manages to creep forward organically in the early stages rather than being held up, their class could make them far more dangerous than their mapped position suggests.
Now So Jake has been off 720 days — monitor his behaviour in the parade ring and his jumping at the early fences, as fitness and sharpness over obstacles after that layoff is entirely unknown.

Boston Jury with Jack Kennedy in the plate is worth tracking from the rear — if the pace quickens at all on the final bend, Kennedy's experience could see him deliver a late run that catches the prominent horses flat-footed.

races.name: WTW Willis Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Nastya
runners_data.note: Five-year form over 3m on Good at Wexford is excellent (3W5P in similar going), De Bromhead's yard in solid form, and she gets to dictate on her own terms; wearing hood and tongue-tie, 62 days off is fine for this type, but the style-fit flag is a reminder she carries risk if the race develops against her.

runners_data.name: Caesar Rock
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who has been a model of consistency at this trip and going, placing in 11 of 15 similar-going runs; Joshua Halford's 7lb claim is a notable asset at 164lbs, and tracking the pace is exactly where he wants to be over 3m on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Goody Four Shoes
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good recently, and Thomas Gibney's yard has had five runners in the last 14 days showing activity; 44 days since last run is fine, and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim helps at the weights — a genuine prominent-style horse in the right position to strike.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's booking for Gordon Elliott (9 winners from 48 in 14 days) is immediately eye-catching; Scalpnagoon has been in excellent form placing in all four recent Good-ground runs, is lightly weighted at OR 114, and ran just 12 days ago suggesting he is in a purple patch.

runners_data.name: Astley
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in this field; Alex Harvey rides and the Paul Traynor yard is quiet (0/1 in 14 days), and with zero wins from nine similar-going runs, Astley needs a stronger pace than Nastya is likely to set and faces an uphill task from the rear.

runners_data.name: Teenage Kiss
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on Good last time for Harry Cobden, who travels over to ride — always worth noting; a natural front-runner by instinct but the map shows her pushed back because there is no room, and whether Cobden elects to push forward regardless will be the key early tactical moment to watch.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Recent form reads PP-657 and this horse has struggled badly over the past year, failing to complete twice; runs from a genuinely prominent position by inclination but has been displaced on the map, and at OR 108 with a quiet trainer strike rate, this is a place confidence is hard to find.

runners_data.name: Duty Bound
runners_data.note: Won twice in similar going (2W3P) and is another true prominent-style horse squeezed into a midfield role by the volume of pace in this field; Jordan Canavan's 7lb claim helps, but a pulled-up run last time and a fall in the form string raise jumping reliability questions over this marathon trip.

runners_data.name: Ceroc
runners_data.note: Won zero of 15 similar-going runs and recent form includes a pulled-up last time; Andrew Slattery's yard has been active (3/32 in 14 days) but Ceroc's own record makes it hard to make a case — a natural prominent type forced further back than suits, compounding an already difficult profile.

races.paceDynamic: Nastya is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with no horse in the field genuinely capable of matching her from the front, she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 3m½f trip on Good ground at Wexford. Caesar Rock, Goody Four Shoes and Scalpnagoon are all legitimate prominent racers who will track closely behind, creating a compact, well-drilled lead group that keeps the race honest without turning it into a war. The field is packed with natural prominent types — Teenage Kiss, Dorans Law, Duty Bound and Ceroc are all genuine front-runners or prominent racers by inclination but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply no room for all of them to race where they want; of those, Teenage Kiss (fresh off a win) and Duty Bound are most likely to push forward and contest for position. The overall shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured gallop, a well-organised chasing pack, and a cramped midfield of horses forced to race out of role — strongly favours prominent/tracking types who can travel smoothly just off the pace and pounce from two out, rather than true hold-up finishers who need a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nastya Dictates, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Nastya bowls along at a fair but unflustered gallop and the horses tracking her in positions two to four get a smooth, uninterrupted journey.
scenarios.body: Nastya sets a rhythm that suits the prominent racers directly behind her, and with the midfield congested by displaced front-runners, the horses who travel sweetly in her slipstream have first run from the second-last fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types (Teenage Kiss, Duty Bound) push forward and create scrimmaging behind the leader, burning out and leaving the race to the established front group.
scenarios.body: Nastya and her immediate trackers benefit from a messy, compressed midfield that never organises a coherent challenge, allowing the front pair to steal vital lengths from the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Teenage Kiss Grabs Position, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Teenage Kiss successfully forces her way to a prominent berth early and Harry Cobden controls the race from close to the front.
scenarios.body: Racing out of her mapped role but genuinely built for prominent racing, Teenage Kiss's recent course-and-distance win shows she can travel powerfully over this trip when given a good position, and a strong jumping display could see her pinch the race from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Nastya goes off too hard under pressure and the pace collapses before the last, allowing hold-up runners to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Astley is the only genuine hold-up type in the field, and a truly run race would theoretically suit her, but the absence of any real pace-forcing dynamic and the fact the midfield is populated by reluctant hold-up horses makes this a low-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Scalpnagoon — Jack Kennedy booking for in-form Elliott yard on a horse who has run 12 days ago and placed in every recent Good-ground start is the most significant jockey/trainer combination in the race; if he travels smoothly just off Nastya, he could be the danger at a bigger price.

Teenage Kiss — Harry Cobden's decision in the opening half-mile will shape the whole race: if he pushes forward to claim a prominent berth, the midfield becomes compressed and chaotic; if he accepts a midfield position, Teenage Kiss is racing well out of role.

Duty Bound and Dorans Law — both are genuine prominent types crowding into the midfield pack; expect scrimmaging and checking between the 2m and 3m marks as these horses try to improve their position, creating interference risk for every runner around them.

Nastya's jumping — at 62 days off and wearing hood and tongue-tie, her jumping fluency early will set the whole complexion of the race; any errors at the first few fences could allow Teenage Kiss or Caesar Rock to move up and take the race away from her on the front end.

Good ground confirmed throughout the card at Wexford — no drying or softening to factor in, meaning OR and class should assert themselves as expected and stamina doubts over 3m½f become the primary selector, particularly for Dorans Law (recent pulls-up) and Duty Bound.

races.name: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Embrace The Day
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer with a win at Wexford in Good 24f and solid course record, but the ⚠ fade flag is a concern over 25f+ in a truly-run race; Gavin Cromwell yard running at 2/41 in the past 14 days adds further caution.

runners_data.name: Midnight Moonshine
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter who should lead unchallenged, though her style fit score of 0.93 flags she is racing slightly out of role for this conditions; recent record of 9th and 11th on Good at similar trips raises doubts about her ability to sustain the gallop she will set.

runners_data.name: North Of Nashville
runners_data.note: Won a 26f Wexford chase on Good and has a second win at similar trips, giving him genuine credentials at this course and distance; Colin Bowe yard has had no winners from 6 runs in the past 14 days, but the horse's form record and natural prominent style are squarely aligned with the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with a win over 26f on Good at Wexford — the most relevant form line in the race — and a place record of 1W3P on similar going; at 10 years old he needs the race to come back to the field but the trip and going suit perfectly.

runners_data.name: Anodandawink
runners_data.note: Well-regarded prominent type with Harry Cobden in the saddle, though the ⚠ fade flag and a prominent field that will crowd his position mean he may not get the clean run he needs; his best form has come at shorter trips on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 23f just 5 days ago, giving her racecourse freshness that not many in this field possess; her 2W3P record across 12 similar-going runs is strong and she handles the trip, though the quick turnaround in an 18-runner chase over fences carries risk.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a win over 24f on Good and placed twice on similar ground — a profile that suits if the race is truly run; Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking, and 16 days since last run keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Oogum Boogum
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win over 24f on Good and placed six times in similar conditions; the 1W7P record in his sim-going history speaks to a horse who runs his race reliably, and he should be able to find a position just off Midnight Moonshine.

runners_data.name: Derby Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with modest form — no wins or places from seven similar-going runs in his history — and a fall on latest outing; hard to make a case for him in this competitive 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Ardaghs Choice
runners_data.note: A true front-runner by nature who is pushed into midfield on the pace map because the prominent positions are over-subscribed; his lengthy absence of 101 days and a form string featuring three URs in five runs are the bigger concerns regardless of where he settles.

runners_data.name: Amburana
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying the ⚠ fade flag, with no wins or places from nine similar-going runs; his form figures of 0,4,3,7,13 over this type of trip suggest he is likely to be outclassed here.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good and has four places from 15 similar-going runs, showing he handles these conditions; however, as a natural prominent type squeezed to midfield by the crowded pace map and ridden by a 7lb claimer, he faces a stiff task to get his preferred position in an 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Barely Made It
runners_data.note: A true hold-up runner shifted to midfield on the map, carrying the ⚠ fade flag; no wins or places from nine similar-going runs and a form string featuring a pulled-up and a fifth suggest limited prospects.

runners_data.name: Captain Kate
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear; a form sequence of 6,6,6,P,P and no wins or places from 13 similar-going runs makes this a very difficult race for her.

runners_data.name: Eddies Pride
runners_data.note: Veteran 12-year-old hold-up type mapped to midfield; no wins or places from 15 similar-going runs and a pulled-up record make him very hard to recommend at any price.

runners_data.name: Tennesse Boy
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer who carries the ⚠ fade flag and is mapped to midfield by congestion; his two most recent runs were both pulled up and he has only one place from 11 similar-going runs, making him a significant risk at this trip.

runners_data.name: Secrecies Of Stone
runners_data.note: Runs without a jockey named, which is a significant practical concern; his form figures of P,9,4,P,P are uninspiring, though he has two historical wins in similar going conditions over this type of trip.

runners_data.name: Chasing Crowns
runners_data.note: Hold-up type carrying the ⚠ fade flag, also running without a listed jockey; a form sequence of P,5,9,3,0 and only one place from 12 similar-going runs gives little confidence over 3m½f.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Moonshine is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner handicap chase over 3m½f at Wexford, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop from flag to finish. Behind her, North Of Nashville, Embrace The Day, Anodandawink, Ladies Well, and Oogum Boogum are all natural prominent racers competing for the same handful of tracking positions, meaning the early order behind the leader will be compressed and competitive — Oogum Boogum and North Of Nashville, both with strong form at this trip and going, appear best placed to actually secure prominent berths. The field also contains more genuine hold-up types than can be fully accommodated at the rear — Ardaghs Choice, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Tennesse Boy, and others are mapped to midfield but are true prominent or hold-up racers squeezed out of role by the sheer weight of pace in this field. With one steady, uncontested gallop set by Midnight Moonshine over an extended trip on Good ground, this race shape strongly favours the horse who can sit just off the pace in a clean prominent position without burning energy in the early scrimmage — patient prominents and genuine hold-up horses with a strong finishing record at this trip are the profile to focus on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moonshine Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Moonshine gets a clean lead and sets an honest but sustainable gallop, allowing the closest trackers to conserve energy.
scenarios.body: Midnight Moonshine dictates throughout at a measured tempo, and the horses positioned just behind her — North Of Nashville and Oogum Boogum — arrive travelling well at the second-last fence with the race to play for. This shape rewards horses who travel prominently without burning fuel early, and both have the course and going form to deliver a strong finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the scrimmage for early prominent positions behind Midnight Moonshine burns out the front rank, leaving the door open for a strong late finisher.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield becomes a waiting game, and any horse that genuinely settles mid-to-rear before picking off fading rivals from the final fence is rewarded. Shantou Show and Mistyburn, both natural hold-up types with course and going form at this trip, are the profiles most likely to benefit from a truly-run race that comes back to them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent trackers overcomes the early congestion to land upsides Midnight Moonshine and grind rivals into submission in the final mile.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners over 3m½f on Good ground, the horse that finds a clean outside position and travels fluently throughout can dominate if the pace is steady enough to keep the hold-up horses out of range. Ladies Well, freshest of the prominent types at only 5 days off a win, and Embrace The Day, with Good-ground course form, are the horses most likely to sustain this kind of effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or unseats disrupt the race and fragment the field, handing an advantage to a horse that finds clear passage mid-race.
scenarios.body: A field of 18 over fences always carries a non-trivial risk of incident, and a scrambled race can produce a winner from an unexpected position. Ardaghs Choice and Fr Gilligansvoyge, true prominents squeezed to midfield by the crowded pace map, could benefit if the race breaks their way and they find themselves tracking the leader despite their mapped position.

watchPoints.text: Midnight Moonshine sets the pace alone but her recent form of 9th and 11th on Good suggests she may not last home — watch for her weakening sharply from two out and gifting the race to patient trackers.

The scramble for prominent positions behind Midnight Moonshine in an 18-runner field over fences is a significant interference risk in the first mile — horses like Anodandawink and Embrace The Day could be badly hampered or lose their pitch entirely.

Ardaghs Choice and Fr Gilligansvoyge are natural front-runners who cannot get their position in this race shape — if either does manage to force their way forward, the pace increases markedly and the dynamics shift against the hold-up horses.

Ladies Well runs just 5 days after her last win — watch whether she travels with the same fluency early; if she does, her race fitness and form at the trip make her dangerous, but any sign of tiredness should be noted.

Shantou Show and Mistyburn are the two hold-up horses with the most relevant course and going form — monitor their positions at halfway to gauge whether a true staying test is developing that will bring them into play late.
